excerpt: The source notes that the cerebellum contains more neurons than the cerebral cortex and many synapses, yet lesions or ablations suggest minimal direct contribution to conscious experience. Figure 4a models a cerebellum-like organization as three strongly interconnected modules with minimal connections among modules; the analysis reveals three separate low-Φ complexes, each with Φ = 20 bits.
overview: This evidence supports the theory's explanation of why computational power and neuron count are insufficient for consciousness. Modular architectures can execute sophisticated specialized routines while failing to form a large integrated complex. The result also clarifies the theory's practical interpretation: direct conscious contribution depends on causal integration pattern, not anatomical size alone.
title: Cerebellar Modules Low Φ
